The presence of multiple corticosteroid pathways connecting to Infectious Anterior Uveitis implies a possible role in reducing inflammation and immune-mediated damage. The high scores in both paths suggest a strong, albeit indirect, mechanistic link, supported by the shared indication of Corneal Ulcer and the downstream association with uveitis. The integration of these pathways supports the hypothesis that Cortisone Acetate may be effective in managing the inflammatory processes underlying Infectious Anterior Uveitis, though further experimental validation is needed to confirm this relationship.
